Author: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili

And
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Pulla Karthik
 Writ Petition No.807 Of 2023
Order:

(per AKS,J) Sri Mohd. Naveed Baghwan, the petitioner, has filed this Habeas Corpus petition on behalf of his brother, Javeed Baghwan, S/o. Yunus Baghwan, the detenu, challenging the detention order vide C.No.715/WRC/CSB-XI/2022, dated 24.12.2022, passed by the respondent No.2-Commissioner of Police, Warangal, whereby, the detenu was detained under Section 3(2) of the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits, Drug- Offenders,
Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders, Land-Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertilizer Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (for short, 'Act 1 of 1986'), and the consequential confirmation order vide G.O.Rt.No.268, General Administration (Spl. (Law & Order)) Department, dated 17.02.2023, passed by the Secretary to 2 AKS,J & PK,J Government, General Administration (Spl. (Law & Order))
Department, Government of Telangana, and to set aside the same.

2. Heard Ms. R. Sowmya Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri S. Mujib Kumar, learned Special Government Pleader, representing the learned Additional Advocate General appearing for the respondents.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner had contended that the brother of the petitioner i.e. detenu was detained by the respondents under the provisions of the Act 1 of 1986 vide impugned detention order, dated 24.12.2022, on the alleged ground that he was involved in Crime No.137 of 2022 of Lingala Ghanpur Police Station, Warangal Police Commissionerate, registered for the offence under Section 8(c) read with 20(b)(ii)(C) of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985.
Learned counsel for the petitioner further contended that the issue whether the provisions under the Act 1 of 1986 can be invoked based upon a solitary crime or not, was considered by a Division Bench of this Court in W.P.No.30726 of 2022, dated 23.09.2022, wherein this Court has set aside the detention order impugned therein with an observation that the provisions under the Act 1 of 1986 cannot be 3 AKS,J & PK,J invoked based upon a solitary crime.

sentences.text: Therefore, appropriate orders be passed in the Writ Petition by setting aside the impugned orders and set free the detenu immediately.
4. On the other hand, the learned Special Government Pleader appearing for the respondents had contended that huge quantity of ganja was seized from the detenu.
The detenu is involving in drug peddling, which affects the general public at large, more particularly, the young generation.
Therefore, the detaining authority was justified in passing the impugned detention order.

Hence,
there are no merits in the Writ Petition and the same is liable to be dismissed.
5.

This Court, having considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties,
is of the view that the issue whether the provisions under the Act 1 of 1986 can be invoked based upon a solitary crime or not, was adjudicated by this Court in W.P.No.30726 of 2022, dated 23.09.2022, wherein this Court has held that the provisions under the Act 1 of 1986 cannot be invoked based upon a solitary crime.

Further, this Court has also taken note 4 AKS,J & PK,J of the fact that the detenu is still in imprisonment on judicial remand and the respondents have invoked the provisions under the Act 1 of 1986, without appreciating the fact whether the detenu was causing any inconvenience to the public or not, as on the date of passing of the impugned detention order.
Therefore, following the aforesaid order, dated 23.09.2022, passed by this Court in W.P.No.30726 of 2022, the impugned orders are liable to be set aside.
6. In the result, the Writ Petition is allowed.

The impugned detention order vide C.No.715/WRC/CSB-XI/2022, dated 24.12.2022, passed by the respondent No.2, and the consequential confirmation order vide G.O.Rt.No.268, General Administration (Spl. (Law & Order))
Department, dated 17.02.2023, passed by the Secretary to Government, General Administration (Spl. (Law & Order)) Department, Government of Telangana, are hereby set aside.
However, it is made clear that since the detenu is already in jail on judicial remand, the question of releasing him would not arise.
However, if the detenu files a bail application, his case has to be considered in accordance with law.
There shall be no order as to costs.
5 AKS,J & PK,J Miscellaneous Petitions, if any, pending in this Writ Petition shall stand closed.
_ __ ABHINAND KUMAR SHAVILI, J _________________ PULLA KARTHIK, J Date: 06-04-2023.
